A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ObjectRelator and provide readable methods, experiments, figures, tables and complete supplementary material. Renamed notation and relocated analyses can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original ObjectRelator and retrained-baseline experiments on Ego-Exo4D, including component ablations, joint training, single-condition testing and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains original Ego-Exo4D experiments and adds HANDAL-X evaluations, generated-description assessments and first-frame-query results.

M1.justification: The core PSALM-based architecture, MCFuse, XObjAlign and two-stage training remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 2.3 adds an inference adaptation: after the first query frame, predictions from previous target-view frames supply subsequent queries. This introduces a limited memory-based procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds HANDAL-X, covering cross-view images of manipulable objects intended for robotics applications, alongside the retained Ego-Exo4D domains. It also evaluates first-frame-only queries and includes target-invisible cases when evaluating visibility accuracy, substantially expanding the tested conditions.

E2.justification: The Ego-Exo4D competitors remain XSegTx, XView-XMem, their combination, SEEM and PSALM; Xmem+XSegTx is an abbreviation. HANDAL-X reuses existing image-based comparators. The relocated fusion ablation omits a repeated PSALM row but retains the base-model comparison in its discussion.

E3.justification: V2 adds LE, CA and VA metrics, evaluating VA on all cases rather than only mutually visible objects. New protocols include HANDAL-X pairing at 100-frame intervals, a description audit sampling 50 frames per scenario, and first-frame inference. The stated learning rate changes from 6e-5 to a choice of 6e-5 or 2e-4, without establishing which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative description-error assessment and a generated-versus-ground-truth text comparison on human-accepted descriptions (Supplementary Table B). It also tests dependence on frame-level queries through first-frame inference (Table F). Existing fusion, alignment, loss-weight, joint-training and single-condition analyses are retained, including material moved to the supplement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The new description-error rates are experimental point estimates, not an added uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises ObjectRelator's Full-set Ego2Exo IoU from 43.9 to 45.4 and adds LE/CA/VA results. New HANDAL-X results include ObjectRelator versus PSALM at 84.7 versus 83.4 after retraining and 42.8 versus 39.9 when transferring from Ego-Exo4D. Supplementary Tables B and F add description-error rates and first-frame IoUs of 37.0/43.7. The revised learning-rate specification prevents treating the updated Full-set score as a confirmed identical-setting gain.

T1.justification: The cross-attention fusion, residual weighting and Euclidean alignment loss retain their mathematical substance. V2's additional forward-pass equations formalize operations already described in v1, while notation is revised. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contributions on ObjectRelator for Ego2Exo/Exo2Ego, efficiency and flexibility. V2 explicitly adds construction of HANDAL-X as a contribution and broadens its abstract and introduction's state-of-the-art claim to two benchmarks. The original two-module method claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning cross-dataset transfer, HANDAL-X's easier conditions and robotics relevance, generated-text accuracy, and the practicality of reducing query annotations. It also explains why visibility accuracy is relatively easy. Existing mechanism explanations, failure categories and the limitation of frame-level modeling largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents HANDAL-X construction, its 44,202 training and 14,074 test samples, and associated training settings and time. It replaces a promised release with a code-availability statement and project link. Most existing implementation details are retained or relocated, although the expanded learning-rate choices lack an experiment-specific mapping.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including HANDAL, CAFuser, XTrack and CamSAM2, and broadens the introductory discussion from video understanding to visual perception. Its central positioning relative to PSALM, universal segmentation and cross-view alignment remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, five contribution items become three, and baseline and method explanations are revised with new notation. Detailed fusion ablations move into reorganized supplementary sections. The title, author information and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn and annotated, Table 2 expands to multiple metrics, and detailed ablations move into the supplement. Existing description-generation and failure-case figures become larger displays. HANDAL-X, text-quality and first-frame tables and a HANDAL-X montage are added; the original extensive Ego2Exo/Exo2Ego montages are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's single benchmark and qualitative reassurance about generated descriptions. HANDAL-X transfer and retraining comparisons, the quantitative text audit, and first-frame testing address important gaps in generalization and practical applicability while preserving the original ablations. HANDAL-X is easier, the text-ambiguity comparison uses only human-accepted descriptions, and the learning-rate revision leaves the updated Full-set score insufficiently explained. These limits temper individual conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
